Report Description///THIS IS A 48HR PHMSA UPDATE TO NRC REPORT 1416254/// THE UPDATE IS AS FOLLOWS: 2ND PARTY CONTRACTOR STILL HOSPITALIZED, THE MATERIAL RELEASED WAS ONLY RESIDUAL GAS IN THE PIPELINE, CROSS COMPRESSION WAS TAKING PRESSURE OFF THE ISOLATED PIPE AND GAS WAS PURGED FROM THE SYSTEM AT THE TIME OF THE FLASH FIRE. THE CALLER STATED DURING A PURGE OF A PIPELINE A FLASH FIRE OCCURRED FOR UNKNOWN REASONS THAT CAUSED TWO (WELDER) WORKERS TO BE INJURED AND SENT TO THE HOSPITAL. ONE OF THE WORKERS WAS RELEASED FROM THE HOSPITAL, AND THE OTHER STAYED OVERNIGHT. -NO FATALITIES.

Medium Affected: UNKNOWN

Skytruth Analysis
COMMAND CENTER (SCC) RECEIVED A REPORT FROM CAL-EMA OF A BARGE FIRE IN MCAVOY MARINA NEAR PITTSBURGH. SCC LAUNCHED STA VJ TO INVESTIGATE AND BRIEFED IMD. LOCAL FIRE DEPT AND HAZMAT UNITS WERE ALREADY ON SCENE. SCC WAS ABLE TO FIND OUT THAT THE BARGE WAS AN OLD WWII BARGE WITH LARGE CANISTERS THAT WERE BEING CUT UP FOR SCRAP EARLIER IN THE DAY. THE FIRE RESULTED FROM CUTTING THAT IGNITED OLD FLAMMABLE RESIDUE IN ONE OF THE OLD DECK MOUNTED TANKS. THE FIRE DEPT PUT THE FIRE OUT AND REPORTED THAT THERE WAS NO APPARENT POLLUTION AND THAT WHAT WAS PRESENT BURNED UP IN THE FIRE. STA VJ STOOD DOWN. IMD WILL HAVE A TEAM INVESTIGATE THE SCENE IN THE MORNING FOR FOLLOW UP.

REPORT DATE: 07-01-2024 REPORT TIME: 1100 UTC REGION: ATLANTIC SUB REGION: MID ATLANTIC U.S. AREA/BLOCK: NORTH ATLANTIC 7004 IMAGE DATE: 06-30-2024 IMAGE TIME: 2234 UTC DATA SOURCE: SENTINEL1A MODE: INTERFEROMETRIC WIDE (IW) VV RESOLUTION: 5X20 METER LOCATION: 40°06"01" N/69°55"03" W AREA: 1.34 SQUARE KILOMETERS CONFIDENCE: HIGH REPORT MAP/GIS FILES: HTTPS://WWW.OSPO.NOAA.GOV/PRODUCTS/OCEAN/MARINEPOLLUTION/ REMARKS: POSSIBLE OIL WAS OBSERVED IN SATELLITE IMAGERY. THIS ANOMALY IS UNCONFIRMED AS OIL. THE ANOMALY APPEARED TO EMANATE NORTHWESTWARD FROM THE SITE OF WRECK 1487, A KNOWN REPEAT SOURCE. THE ANOMALY MEASURED APPROXIMATELY 3.5 NMI IN LENGTH, AND UP TO 0.25 NMI IN WIDTH, AND HAD A DISTINCT, DARK APPEARANCE AGAINST ITS BACKGROUND. WINDS AT THE TIME OF THE IMAGE WERE FROM THE S AT AROUND 12 KTS. UNCERTAINTIES: THE ANOMALY EDGES WERE NOT PARTICULARLY WELL-DEFINED.
